source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) approval is REQUIRED when: (1) Any foreign individual, company, or NRI seeks to obtain biological resources from India for research, commercial utilization, or bio-survey; (2) Any person seeks to transfer results of research relating to Indian biological resources to foreigners; (3) Any person applies for intellectual property rights (patents) in or outside India on inventions based on Indian biological resources or traditional knowledge. Indian citizens and companies may access biological resources for research purposes with intimation to State Biodiversity Board, but commercial use still requires NBA approval.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: Form I is used for seeking approval of NBA for access to biological resources and/or associated traditional knowledge for research or commercial utilization. The form requires: applicant details, description of biological resource sought, geographical location of collection, intended use (research/commercial), details of any traditional knowledge involved, proposed benefit-sharing arrangement, and proof of prior informed consent from local communities where applicable.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: Form III is used for seeking prior approval of NBA before applying for intellectual property rights. This form must be filed BEFORE filing a patent application if the invention uses Indian biological resources or traditional knowledge. The form requires: details of the biological resource used, how and where it was obtained, description of the invention, proposed IP rights, and benefit-sharing proposal. Filing a patent application without Form III approval can result in penalty up to Rs 50 lakh.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) fees under NBA regulations: For commercial utilization, benefit sharing is 3-5% of annual gross ex-factory sale price of the product. For obtaining biological resources, a one-time fee of Rs 500 is prescribed as lumpsum benefit sharing. For applicants who already pay benefit sharing under other NBA forms, additional fees are waived. For biological resources with high conservation or economic value (listed in Annex-I), benefit sharing is 25% higher than standard rates.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: Section 6 of Biological Diversity Act 2002: Any person applying for any intellectual property right in or outside India for any invention based on research or information on biological resources obtained from India must obtain prior approval of NBA. This is mandatory even if the biological resource was legally obtained. Violation can lead to: (1) Rejection of patent application, (2) Revocation of granted patent, (3) Penalty up to Rs 50 lakh, (4) Imprisonment up to 5 years for serious violations.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: India is a party to the Nagoya Protocol on Access to Genetic Resources and Benefit Sharing. This means: (1) When using biological resources from India, users must comply with Indian ABS laws; (2) When Indian researchers access genetic resources from other Nagoya Protocol countries, they must comply with that country's ABS laws; (3) The internationally recognized certificate of compliance (IRCC) issued by NBA serves as evidence of legal access; (4) Other countries can check compliance through the ABS Clearing House.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: For AYUSH products using Indian biological resources: If the product is based on codified traditional knowledge (found in classical texts like Charaka Samhita, Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia), benefit sharing may be reduced or waived as this knowledge is in public domain. However, NBA approval is still required if seeking IP rights on any modification or new formulation. For wild-collected medicinal plants, ensure sourcing from sustainable legal sources and maintain documentation of collection permits from forest authorities.

source: Biological Diversity Act 2002 and NBA Guidelines (Curated)
text: Penalties under Biological Diversity Act 2002: Contravention of Section 3 (access without approval), Section 4 (transfer without approval), or Section 6 (IP without approval) is punishable with imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine up to Rs 10 lakh, or both. If the offence is by a company, every person in charge of the company is deemed guilty. For Ayurvedic/pharmaceutical companies, non-compliance can result in patent invalidation in addition to criminal penalties.
